history.period: Mid-19th century, about 150 years old (one source says 1928 AD - conflict, verify)
history.summary: NON-HINDU FLAG: this is a JAIN temple (Svetambara, per trawell.in), NOT a Hindu temple. Keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset. Founded about 150 years ago by Raghunath Prasad Bhandari, inspired by the famous glass temple of Kolkata Bara Bazaar (the temple marked its 150th anniversary in 2025-26 per knocksense). Built in traditional style but entirely adorned with glass and mirror work - walls, pillars, ceilings and arches, marble floors, and stained-glass murals depicting Jain scriptures; the Tirthankara statues stand on a large marble platform under ornate canopies, and a garden with sculptures of Jain deities adjoins the temple. DATE CONFLICT: kanpurtourism.in says mid-19th century (about 150 years), airial.travel says 1928 AD - verify. DEDICATION NOTE: trawell.in titles it for Dharmanath (16th Tirthankara) while most sources say Mahavira and the 24 Tirthankaras - verify.

name: Jain Glass Temple, Kanpur
town: Kanpur (Maheshwari Mohal, General Ganj - behind Kamala Tower)
town_description: The temple stands in Maheshwari Mohal, General Ganj locality of Kanpur city, behind the well-known Kamala Tower - about 3.5 km from Kanpur Central. General Ganj is an old commercial quarter of the city; the temple's shimmering glass exterior makes it a landmark tourist spot as well as a Jain worship centre.
